title: First major international Zurbarán retrospective since 1987 opens at the Musée du Louvre
summary: Francisco de Zurbarán, along with Diego Velázquez and Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, is considered one of the greatest Spanish painters of the 17th century. At first considered a Caravaggista with a focus on monastic ascetism, he was gradually recognised in the 20th century as a prodigious colourist and celebrated for his distinctive personal style, which married a simple treatment of volumes with striking naturalism. Though Zurbarán has been the subject of numerous exhibitions over the last ten years, the last large-scale international presentation to focus on his work had been the joint exhibition Zurbarán, mounted by the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Grand Palais in 1987–1988. title: LA Art Show returns January 6-10 with GLAAD as new 2027 Charity Partner
summary: LA Art Show , Los Angeles’ longest-established art fair, returns to the Los Angeles Convention Center’s West Hall January 6–10, 2027, for its 32nd edition, ushering in Los Angeles’ 2027 art season with a diverse roster of galleries and international perspectives while reflecting the city’s uniquely multicultural creative landscape. The fair’s new 2027 charity partner and beneficiary is GLAAD, an inspiring nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing LGBTQ acceptance and inclusive representation across all forms of media. Fifteen percent of ticket proceeds will benefit GLAAD and its important work. LA Art Show also welcomes official ticketing partner Tixr, a global leader in ticketing and live event commerce known for its innovative, high tech platform, which offers a seamless, modern ticketing experience for attendees. title: Christie's opens October Jewels Online sale featuring over 200 fine jewelry lots
summary: Christie's will present Jewels Online this October, open for bidding from 6-15 October online and on view at Christie's Rockefeller Center galleries from 8-12 October. The sale showcases more than 200 lots, including a distinguished selection of important diamonds, vibrant colored gemstones, and fine jewelry. Highlighting the sale is a significant assemblage of signed jewels from leading houses such as Bulgari, Cartier, David Webb, Harry Winston, Tiffany & Co., and Van Cleef & Arpels as well as several important private collections. Jewels Online is led by a round brilliant-cut Diamond Ring of 8.17 carats (estimate: $250,000-350,000). Additional top lots include a Sapphire and Diamond Ring of 25.29 carats (estimate: 70,000-90,000), a pair of Harry Winston Diamond Cluster Earrings (estimate: 40,000-60,000), and a Tiffany & Co., Jean Schlumberger Sapphire and Diamond 'Cooper' Bracelet (estimate: $30,000-50,000). title: Uncle Roy brings Roy Blakey's life in skating, photography and LGBTQ+ history to NewFest
summary: After a festival run that began with its world premiere at the Thessaloniki International Documentary Festival, Keri Pickett’s Uncle Roy will have its New York City premiere at NewFest, New York’s largest LGBTQ+ film festival, on Sunday, October 18 at 6:45 p.m. at SVA Theatre. The feature-length documentary traces the extraordinary life of Roy Blakey, Pickett’s uncle, whose career moved between military service, international ice shows, photography and one of the world’s largest archives devoted to theatrical figure skating. In his final years, as Blakey developed severe dementia, Pickett became his caregiver while racing to preserve the photographs, documents and objects that recorded nearly a century of personal and cultural history. Born in Oklahoma in 1930, Blakey became fascinated by figure skating as a child after seeing Olympic champion Sonja Henie in the 1941 film Sun Valley Serenade. title: American Folk Art Museum presents landmark exhibition 'Locating Girlhood' for U.S. semiquincentennial
summary: This fall, the American Folk Art Museum presents Locating Girlhood: Place and Identity in Early American “Schoolgirl” Art, a major exhibition bringing together works from across the field. Presented during the nation’s semiquincentennial, Locating Girlhood reexamines the often-overlooked artistic production of girls and young women in eighteenth- and nineteenth-century America, highlighting their sustained engagement with representations of place long before the emergence of more widely recognized traditions of American landscape art. Drawing on loans from institutions and private collections across the United States and Canada, the exhibition offers one of the most significant explorations of early American girls’ artistic achievement ever assembled. “The American Folk Art Museum has long championed the creative achievements of American girls and young women,” said Jason T. title: Two-volume edition published by Zander Galerie pairs On Kawara and Lewis Baltz
summary: Zander Galerie announced the forthcoming publication On Kawara | Lewis Baltz, a two-volume edition dedicated to seminal early works of both artists: On Kawara's Today (1968–79) and I Met series are explored in one volume, the other centres on Lewis Baltz's The Tract Houses (1969–71) and The Prototype Works (1967–76). Published by Zander Galerie in collaboration with Verlag der Buchhandlung Walther und Franz König and edited by Thomas Zander, the edition comprises two autonomous volumes, each features an essay by Benjamin H. D. Buchloh. title: Georgia Museum of Art receives five regional awards
summary: The Georgia Museum of Art at the University of Georgia recently received five awards from the Southeastern Museums Conference (SEMC). The awards were presented at the SEMC Annual Meeting Awards Luncheon on September 30, 2026, in Winston Salem, North Carolina. The museum will also be featured in the Winter 2026 Edition of “Inside SEMC.” In the Exhibition Competition, the museum received a gold award in the over $25,000 budget category for “We, Too, Are Made of Wonders.” Organized by Ciel Rodriquez, curatorial assistant in contemporary art, and inspired by Ada Limón’s poem “In Praise of Mystery,” the exhibition featured historic, modern and contemporary art from the museum’s collection focusing on awe, wonder and the night sky. title: Judd Foundation reconstructs seminal 1993 Yun Hyong-keun exhibition at 101 Spring Street
summary: Judd Foundation presents Yun Hyong-keun, an exhibition of paintings by Yun Hyong-keun at 101 Spring Street in New York. The exhibition reconstructs Hyong-keun Yun 1993, one of the artist’s first solo exhibitions in the United States, organized by Donald Judd and Locks Gallery. Yun Hyong-keun is presented in recognition of the public opening of the Yun Hyong-keun House and organized in partnership with the Estate of Yun Hyong-keun. Yun Hyong-keun (1928–2007) is one of the most important South Korean painters of the twentieth century. Beginning in the 1970s, Yun employed a technique of superimposing pigment and color on unprimed canvas. Later that decade, he began using ultramarine and umber as the sole colors in his paintings, soaking and spreading the paint directly on cloth or linen canvas. title: Marco Maggi explores generic materials and cultural criticism at Bienvenu Steinberg & C
summary: Bienvenu Steinberg & C presents Higher Perplexity, Marco Maggi’s 11th solo exhibition in New York. The exhibition will be on view from October 8 through November 14, 2026. Maggi’s abstract language favors generic formats and materials. Devoid of any symbolism or signification, his vocabulary refers to the way information is processed in a global yet increasingly myopic era. Composed of linear pathways reminiscent of circuit boards, aerial views, genetic engineering and nervous systems, his drawings and sculptures encode the world and turn abstraction into cultural criticism. Born in Montevideo, Uruguay in 1957, Marco Maggi lives and works in New York and Uruguay. His work has been shown extensively throughout the United States, Latin America and Europe. title: First Chicanx art museum exhibition in Switzerland opens with 'Los Four & Friends'
summary: For the first time in Switzerland, “Los Four & Friends” presents an exhibition of Chicanx art in a museum. It showcases the artistic production of Los Four, a Chicano art collective active in California between 1973 and 1984. Centring the history of the collective, the exhibition expands into an exploration of Chicanx art in Los Angeles, from the 1970s to the present. “Chicano”, “Chicana” or “Chicanx” is a self-defined identity adopted by people of Mexican descent in the United States. Reclaimed during the 1960s Chicano civil rights movement (“El Movimiento”), the term became a political and cultural expression of pride in Mexican heritage and a resistance to discrimination. “El Movimiento” fought for economic justice, political representation, educational reform, and the reclamation of Mexican-American identity. title: Artcurial highlights Orientalist masterworks and African modernism in flagship Marrakech sale
summary: Artcurial returns to the elegant setting of La Mamounia on December 30, 2026, for a new edition of A Moroccan Winter, an event that holds special significance this year as it marks the 15th edition of the Majorelle & his Contemporaries auction. The first section of this auction pays tribute to Jacques Majorelle with a collection of some twenty works, alongside artists such as José Cruz-Herrera and Bernard Boutet de Monvel. This section also features works by 19th-century Orientalist artists such as Frederick Arthur Bridgman, Eugène Girardet, Arthur von Ferraris, and Eugène Flandin, including a magnificent view of Constantinople. title: Pace at Frieze London: Marina Perez Simão solo presentation
summary: Pace will present a solo booth of new paintings by Brazilian artist Marina Perez Simão at Frieze London 2026. Marking a novel direction in the artist’s practice, the body of paintings on view explores the perceptual possibilities of color through three distinct spectrums of magenta, blue, and gray. Known for her work across painting, watercolor, installation, and drawing, Perez Simão merges interior and exterior landscapes in abstract, undulating compositions alive with movement, color, and light. In her paintings for Frieze London, she activates subtle shifts in tone to create works that change with the viewer’s movement and perspective, at times revealing unexpected variations in hue and temperature. Though they are more focused in chromatic scope than her previous works, as Perez Simão describes, “they are not really monochromes. Instead, I worked with families of blues, grays, and pinks so that each painting behaves as though it contains a full palette.” Pace

title: Artcurial to auction historic personal collection of Aéropostale pioneer Jean Mermoz
summary: On November 3rd, 2026, Artcurial will present at auction for the first time an exceptional collection of personal items and memorabilia belonging to Jean Mermoz (1901–1936), which have been kept by his family since his death. Offering a genuine insight into the private life of one of the greatest figures of the Aéropostale, this sale traces the extraordinary life of a man who became a legend. His leather coat worn in the Andes, his parachute engraved with his name, his aviator’s goggles and his second lieutenant’s cap will be auctioned alongside mementoes from the Aéropostale and his childhood, such as his christening clothes and school drawings. Letters telling his many accidents, as well as a rare photographic portrait of Antoine de Saint-Exupéry inscribed “to my old friend Mermoz”, will feature in this auction including over 200 lots. title: Sophie Calle turns her birthday into an artwork as MAXXI prepares major Rome exhibition
summary: Sophie Calle is bringing her deeply personal investigations of intimacy, memory, absence and loss to Rome this October, beginning with two unusual events that blur the boundaries between private ritual and public participation ahead of the opening of her major MAXXI exhibition. On October 9 — Calle’s birthday — the French conceptual artist will present The Birthday Conference at the MAXXI Auditorium. Rather than asking visitors to purchase a conventional ticket, Calle has proposed a more personal form of admission: each member of the audience is invited to bring her a birthday present. The gesture transforms what might otherwise have been a museum lecture into the kind of participatory experiment that has defined Calle’s practice for nearly five decades. title: Rekha Rodwittiya celebrates 20th solo exhibition with Sakshi Gallery
summary: Home is wherever you are marks Rekha Rodwittiya's 20th solo with Sakshi Gallery. Spread across two floors and spanning oil on canvas, embroidery, carpets, photography, and watercolours, the exhibition brings together a wide-ranging body of work that reflects the artist's sustained engagement with memory, lived experience, history and the narratives of women. Also presented for the first time is a series of photographs taken by Rodwittiya in 1978, while studying under the tutelage of Professor Jyoti Bhatt. Rodwittiya's densely layered compositions often create spaces in which personal and collective histories intersect. As the artist observes, “My area of focus resembles a garden—a tiny plot of land that I continually cultivate, till, plow, and harvest.” This process of accumulation and reconfiguration is evident in the ongoing series Home is wherever

title: Bunkier Sztuki collection of Polish contemporary art travels to Reykjavík
summary: The exhibition features exclusively works from the collection of Bunkier Sztuki, which houses one of the strongest collections of Polish contemporary art in Europe. The exhibition includes photographs, paintings, sculptures, and installations by thirty artists from Poland. The body is at the forefront of the exhibition, which brings together works created predominantly in the 21st century, a period marked by rapid social change, technological advancement, and evolving ideas about the body, identity, and existence. The exhibition directs attention to the body as a living process rather than a fixed entity. It is shaped by environment, technology, social norms, and histories, and is always in relation to other bodies, other lives, and other worlds. title: Maureen Paley presents new exhibition of bronze and raw clay sculptures by Rebecca Warren
summary: Maureen Paley presents an exhibition of new sculptures by Rebecca Warren in both Bethnal Green gallery spaces. “I imagined this show as a retrospective being made by a slightly different version of me. Like making your work now, in the usual way, but also oddly in the mode of a retrospective, so that each thing shifts between two time frames. Everything seems familiar but strange somehow, right but not quite right. Like there’s another version of you who’s doing it simultaneously...” -- Rebecca Warren, 2026 There Will Be Another You (2026) is a bronze life-size reclining nude female, dropped or resting, limbs melting or morphing, exposed sinews and wires, two right arms, no left arm, a mix of blur and focus in the rendering. title: MOCA Tucson opens Clifford Prince King's first museum exhibition in the Southwest
summary: MOCA (Museum of Contemporary Art) Tucson presents After Heaven, a solo exhibition by artist Clifford Prince King that features a new series of photographs, a photo-installation, and a video work. It is the artist’s first museum exhibition in the Southwest. King’s approach to photography is intuitive and diaristic: for him, making a photograph is a way to understand himself, his subjects, and the world around him. He captures subtle, everyday moments that brim with connection, tenderness, and care, registering the expansiveness of Black queer personhood. His photographs often feature friends, lovers, and the artist himself; for After Heaven, King directs his focus to family, place, and landscape in Tucson, Arizona, where he grew up, and nearby Sahuarita on his family’s ranch. title: Castellani Art Museum presents a solo exhibition by AI poet Sasha Stiles
summary: The Castellani Art Museum of Niagara University presents Sasha Stiles: STANZA, a solo exhibition by internationally recognized poet, artist, and AI researcher Sasha Stiles, on view through April 25, 2027. An opening reception will be held Thursday, October 8, 2026. The exhibition is curated by Jess Minicucci. Presented following Stiles’s recent exhibition A LIVING POEM at The Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) in New York, STANZA expands the artist’s ongoing investigation of poetry, artificial intelligence, and the evolving relationship between human and machine. At CAM, Stiles brings these ideas into an immersive gallery environment, inviting visitors to experience poetry not simply as something read on a page, but as something that can be entered, heard, seen, and inhabited. title: DC Moore Gallery presents 'The Meadow's Edge', a new solo exhibition by Eric Aho
summary: DC Moore Gallery presents Eric Aho: The Meadow’s Edge. In this exhibition, Eric Aho further explores the meadow subject introduced in his 2024 exhibition, Wild Meadow. Returning to the meadow at sunrise, twilight, and throughout the seasons, Aho catches glimpses of transient atmospheres between light and darkness, snow and thaw. Alongside nocturnal paintings of fireflies, moonlit forests, and reimagined Dutch still lifes, Aho addresses the oncoming night and the mysterious forms of illumination therein. Together, these works present an inquiry into the borders of observation and imagination, perception found at the edges of spaces and forms. title: Heritage Auctions names Erik Myers Vice President of Modern Cards
summary: Heritage Auctions announces the hiring of Erik Myers as Vice President of Modern Cards, adding a veteran with 19 years of experience in the trading card space and 18 years of experience in project management to its Sports department. Myers brings a combination of deep hobby knowledge and organizational expertise to the world’s leading sports auctioneer. His experience in the trading card community provides a strong foundation for connecting with collectors and consignors, while his project management background adds a disciplined approach to coordinating complex initiatives and guiding them from start to finish. “Erik’s extensive experience in the sports card collecting community and his knowledge of modern cards make him an outstanding addition to our team,” says Chris Ivy, Heritage’s Director of Sports Auctions. “He understands

title: Khalif Tahir Thompson explores memory, tragedy, and Black American identity in new London exhibition
summary: Victoria Miro presents Send in the Clowns, an exhibition of new paintings by Khalif Tahir Thompson. This is the gallery’s first solo presentation of Thompson’s work since announcing representation of the artist. Born and based in Brooklyn, Khalif Tahir Thompson invites viewers into the everyday lives of his subjects through vibrant domestic scenes, full of texture and pattern that create an expansive form of portraiture, both individual and collective, weaving through time.
